name: The Porthier household
head: porthier_joseph

arrival.note: NOT ATTESTED. He is a member of the agency establishment under Owen, whose agency runs from 1831; the Porthier family is at Chicago earlier. 1830 is the earliest year this project can argue and it cites nothing.

party_size_on_arrival.note: Not attested in anything this project holds.

origin.note: DRAWN FROM A SURVIVORSHIP SAMPLE. No source says where this household came from. The region is drawn from the birthplaces of the seventy Old Settlers who registered an arrival at or before 1835 — a self-selected roll set down forty-four years later that over-represents the men who stayed and prospered, as the town model's own open questions say. It is the only origin distribution this project holds and this value is drawn from it, not measured.

replaceable_by.match: a source that says where this household came from

reason_for_coming.value: A mechanic's trade in a town that had few of it
reason_for_coming.note: ARGUED FROM THIS HOUSEHOLD'S OWN RECORDED TRADE, WHICH IS NOT ITS MOTIVE. The head is recorded as blacksmith, and this names the documented draw that trade answered in this town in this decade. It does not claim to know why these people came. Which of these draws brought this household is not recorded, and no committed source apportions the town between them.

basis.note: arrival_fill.trade_reasons.a_mechanics_trade — the head's recorded trade is evidence about this household, and the draw it answered is the reason the record will carry until a source states one.

replaceable_by.match: a source that says why this household came, or a committed source that apportions the town's arrivals between the land sales, the canal and the harbour works

lives_at.note: Not attested in anything this project holds.

works_at.note: The same shop as McKee. Two named men at one anvil is the only documented workplace pairing in the parcel.

present_on_scene_date.note: T-0478 resolves the earlier uncertainty. Pioneer History of Milwaukee dates Joseph Porthier leaving Chicago with Horace Chase on February 27, 1835; after a brief return to Chicago for means, Porthier left again March 21 and reached Milwaukee March 23. That dated migration is before the July 1 scene date.

persons.name: Joseph Porthier

occupation.note: Striker to the government blacksmith at the Indian agency - the man who swings the sledge for the smith. Andreas names him in the agency establishment under Owen: 'David McKee as blacksmith, and Joseph Porthier as striker'. The occupation vocabulary has no separate entry for a striker and blacksmith is the trade he was in.

persons.note: A WAGE-EARNING ASSISTANT, WHICH THIS DATASET HAS ALMOST NONE OF, and a member of a family the 1833 treaty names: the schedule of payments in lieu of reservations carries 'Victoire Porthier and her children, $700'. Andreas's chapter on the early settlement treats the Mirandeau and Porthier families together as part of the French and mixed-descent community at Chicago. T-0478 adds a dated February-March 1835 migration to Milwaukee, resolving scene-date absence without inferring ancestry from the surname.

resident_research.evidence_for: Pioneer History of Milwaukee supplies a materially tighter migration chronology than the existing record: Joseph Porthier left Chicago with Horace Chase on February 27, 1835, briefly returned to Chicago for means, then left again March 21 and reached Milwaukee March 23. This places his removal before the July 1 scene date.

roles.note: THE BOUND IS THE SOURCE'S, NOT THE MAN'S. This role is carried by the card's 1835 occupation block and is dated by what the cited source or sources are ABOUT, which is why `precision` can be no better than the span they cover. The span reaches 1835, so this role stands in the scene-date view. The printing the trade was read off is not on the card and is fetched by T-1254.

basis.note: Drawn from the 1840 Chicago schedule's column 'free white males 20 under 30', one of its male bands, conditioned on `named_on_a_roll_15_and_over` because the person is named in their own right on any other roll this layer was minted from - a letter list, a subscription, a court docket, a trade notice - or carries a role, a trade, a marriage or a parenthood.

replaceable_by.match: a source that states this person's age, their birth year, or an interval either can be read out of

age_band.note: AN AGE BAND, NEVER A YEAR. No source this project holds bears on when this person was born, so the band is drawn from the only committed sex by age distribution the project has - the 1840 Chicago schedule, five years after the scene and a town twice the size - seeded by this person's own id ('porthier_joseph:age_bands_1840'). AND THE CONDITIONING IS THE MODEL'S, NOT A SOURCE'S: that a roll naming a person in their own right names somebody 15 or over. The 1840 schedule counts a child as a tally inside a household and never as a correspondent; 15 rather than 20 because an apprentice or a journeyman stands on a trade roll. No source states this rule. No exact year is written, because a year drawn from a decadal band would read as a record of a birth.

research_note: THE ONLY DOCUMENTED STRIKER IN THE DATASET, and a reminder of how the documented population is skewed. Andreas names hundreds of proprietors and perhaps a dozen employees; this man is in the record only because the agency's payroll was a matter of federal accounting. T-0478 found a dated migration sequence: Porthier left Chicago February 27, 1835, briefly returned for means, left again March 21, and reached Milwaukee March 23. STANDING CONSTRAINT. AGENTS.md: the final removal of the Potawatomi from Chicago occurred in August 1835, inside this project's first target year and six weeks AFTER the scene date; Native presence, representation and depiction are not research gaps to be filled by inference, and v1 ships no human figures at all. This record states only what named sources say about a named person. It carries review_required so that no scene containing it can be marked released before the consultation the project has committed to.
